against: f17ae369 (claude/peaceful-hamilton-59zdbb), the tree clean, read before any code of this area changed. A copy of that tree, node_modules linked, is the scratchpad's arion/base, where the reproductions below were run (arion/probe-before.txt).
writtenBefore: This checklist was written after the research (AR0, which reads and changes nothing in the repository) and before the first change to code, content, a test or a tool.
reachability: Every new life is made at Yale in New Haven. Creation's Before Yale keeps an account at a bank in the country the student lived in (systems/homeaccount.ts): a Reykjavík-raised student keeps Arion's Veltureikningur, opened before Yale, its debit card charged on the life's first night, 25 August 2026 at midnight in New Haven (04:00 in Reykjavík), and Close It (bank.close_current) closes it once its savings are closed and Chase is primary. So the first charge, the renewals and a close are reached in play. An Arion account opened in the life is reached only by a quick-save life in Iceland (a FIXTURE), as no played life opens an Icelandic account.

research.searched: 2026-10-16, a focused search: Arion's price list, payment-account fee sheet, general terms (which carry its card terms), its debit-card pages in Icelandic and English, the official glossary of payment-account terms; Iceland's Act on Payment Services no. 114/2021 from the Official Journal (althingi.is still answers 403, and web.archive.org is blocked by this container's egress policy); the amending acts the Official Journal's search finds for 2022 to 2026; the EEA incorporation of Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (EFTA's EEA-Lex); the Directive's art. 55 (legislation.gov.uk; EUR-Lex answered 202 with a challenge). Every source and what it says is in the result, arion-result.json, research.
confirmed: The amount and the age: 950 kr a year from 24, 0 kr at 23 and under (Arion's Gjaldskrá greiðslureikninga, Veltureikningur, 07.05.2026; Verðskrá einstaklinga 13.1 and 13.1.1, valid from 07.05.2026; its debit-card pages).
That it's a fee paid once a year (the official glossary, B-deild no. 485/2023: 'Gjald sem viðskiptavinur greiðir reikningsveitanda einu sinni á ári fyrir debetkort').
Who pays and from where: the account holder, debited from the account holder's account (Arion's general terms 18.7.1.15, ch. 5).
That Arion's card terms are a framework contract under Act 114/2021 (its terms 1.1), and that its separate debit-card terms ceased with the general terms (ch. 11).

What a close owes whatever the timing, for a consumer: Act 114/2021 art. 57(4): regular payments are collected after a termination in proportion to its effective date, and fees paid in advance are refunded in proportion; art. 57(2), termination free of charge; art. 41, derogation only where the user isn't a consumer; art. 113, it implements Directive (EU) 2015/2366 as incorporated by EEA Joint Committee Decision 165/2019 of 14 June 2019; art. 115, in force 1 November 2021.
notConfirmed: Whether the 950 kr pays for the card year ahead or the year past, and on what day it's charged: none of Arion's documents read, nor the glossary, nor the Act, says.
How Arion counts the proportional share (days, months), and whether the year runs from the card's issue, the account's opening or a fixed date.
Whether art. 57 has been amended since 2021: the consolidated text couldn't be read; the amending acts the Official Journal's search found don't touch it.

rule: The Act settles what a close owes whatever the timing (art. 57(4)), so that part is the source's. The timing isn't settled, so the brief's labelled, configurable SLATE simulation assumption: ARION_CARD_YEAR (content/banks-thirteen.ts), default 'ahead': each charge pays for the card year it opens, the first on the account's first night in the life, renewed on the same date a year on in Reykjavík's calendar; on a close the days of that card year left come back in proportion, rounded half up to the whole króna, against Bank Fees. 'behind' (each charge pays for the year it ends, and a close charges the days used) is implemented and tested as the setting's other value, so a later source replaces it by one word. Each card year is settled by the rule it was opened under (Account.cardYearRule), so changing the setting never charges or refunds a year twice.
